officialName: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (PM-USP CSSS)

authority.name: Ministry of Education, Government of India

summary: Merit scholarship for students above the 80th percentile in their Class XII board, pursuing a regular degree course, with family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh a year.

benefits.description: Scholarship at graduation level for the first three years of a college or university course
benefits.conditions: Students pursuing technical courses such as B.Tech or B.Engg receive this rate for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd year.
Students on five-year or integrated professional courses receive this rate in the 4th and 5th year; students on technical courses such as B.Tech receive it in the 4th year.

eligibility.notes: Research draft only. Current-cycle applicability, exact conditions, exceptions, document wording, and completeness require independent human review. Do not use for student assessments.

children.reason: The scheme requires a student to be above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in the relevant stream from their own Board of Examination in Class XII. That percentile depends on board-wide results, not on a student's own marks.
children.checkHint: Check your board's merit list or the National Scholarship Portal for your stream's cut-off.

children.reason: The course must be at a college or institution recognised by the All India Council for Technical Education and the respective regulatory bodies concerned, and the institution must hold a valid AISHE code.
children.checkHint: Confirm your institution's AISHE code at aishe.gov.in and ask your institution about its recognition.

documents.title: Income certificate
documents.notes: The guidelines state that an income certificate is required only for fresh applicants.

documents.title: Class XII board examination result
documents.notes: The guidelines base selection on Class XII board results and verify credentials through DigiLocker, but they do not list the documents a student uploads. Check the National Scholarship Portal for the current document list.

documents.title: Bank account in the student's own name, for Direct Benefit Transfer
documents.notes: Prepare this for the official portal only. Schemelog never asks for account numbers.

applicationSteps.title: Read the current guidelines and the timelines published on the National Scholarship Portal
applicationSteps.description: The guidelines state that the portal provides the opening and closing timelines, and that the latest timeline guidance is published there.

applicationSteps.title: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal
applicationSteps.description: Applications are received online only. Credentials such as category and educational qualifications are verified through DigiLocker.

applicationSteps.title: Have your application verified by your institution, then by the state authority
applicationSteps.description: Online applications are verified at two levels: by the institution where the student is studying, and then by the concerned State Higher Education Department or the nominated State Nodal Agency.
